Selling Online

How to Start Selling Online in Bangladesh: Website, Payments and Delivery

Want to sell online in Bangladesh? A practical guide to choosing products, building your shop, taking bKash and card payments, delivery and marketing.

NM Nipun Mitra ·26 October 2026 ·2 min read

More people than ever want to sell online in Bangladesh — handmade products, clothing, electronics, food, courses and services. Many start with a Facebook page, and that’s a fine first step. But as orders grow, answering every message by hand, tracking payments and arranging deliveries quickly becomes a full-time job.

I’ve built e-commerce and business websites, including an electronics store with WordPress and WooCommerce. Here’s a practical path from your first sale to a proper online shop.

1. Choose what to sell — and who to sell to

The best products solve a clear problem for a specific group of people. Check demand before you invest: what are people already searching for, asking about in groups, or buying from competitors? A focused niche is easier to market than “a bit of everything”.

2. Social media page or your own website?

Social commerce is fast to start and great for discovery. Your own website adds what social media can’t:

  • Customers can browse and order 24/7 without waiting for a reply.
  • Clear prices, stock and product details build trust.
  • Your shop can be found on Google.
  • You own the customer relationship — not an algorithm.

Most successful shops use both: social media for reach, the website for orders.

3. Build your online shop

  • Fast product pages with clear photos, prices, sizes and stock.
  • A short checkout with guest ordering — no forced accounts.
  • Mobile-first design, because most of your customers will shop on their phones.
  • An admin panel for products, orders and stock.
  • Click-to-call and WhatsApp for customers who still want to ask before buying.

WordPress with WooCommerce is a solid, affordable start. A custom build makes sense once you need special features or serious traffic.

4. Payments: offer what customers already use

Cash on delivery is still common, but online payment reduces fake orders and returns. Integrate mobile financial services like bKash and Nagad and card payments through a payment gateway, and show the total — including delivery — before checkout. Fewer surprises means fewer abandoned carts.

5. Delivery and fulfilment

  • Work with reliable courier services and compare coverage, pickup and cash-on-delivery handling.
  • Set clear delivery charges and times for inside and outside Dhaka.
  • Send order confirmations and tracking updates by SMS or WhatsApp.
  • Publish a simple, fair return policy — it increases trust.

6. Marketing that brings repeat customers

  • Run focused social media ads to people likely to buy.
  • Use SEO so your product and category pages show up on Google.
  • Collect reviews and photos from happy customers.
  • Build a customer list for offers and new arrivals.

7. Trust, legal and the boring essentials

Keep your trade licence and business details in order, show your real contact information and address, and publish clear terms, privacy and refund policies. These small things make first-time buyers far more comfortable ordering.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a website to sell online in Bangladesh?

You can start on Facebook or Instagram, but your own website builds trust, lets customers order at any time without waiting for replies, ranks on Google, and keeps your business independent of social media algorithms.

Which payment methods should an online shop in Bangladesh accept?

Most shops offer cash on delivery plus mobile financial services such as bKash and Nagad, and card payments through a payment gateway. Offering the methods your customers already use reduces abandoned orders.

WordPress/WooCommerce or a custom e-commerce website?

WooCommerce is a cost-effective start for most small shops. A custom build makes sense when you need special features, high traffic performance, or deep integration with your inventory, delivery or accounting systems.
